olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Circles $\omega_1,\omega_2$ intersect at $X,Y$. Line $\ell_1$ through center of $\omega_1$ meets $\omega_2$ at $P,Q$; $\ell_2$ through center of $\omega_2$ meets $\omega_1$ at $R,S$. If $P,Q,R,S$ are concyclic, prove their circle's center lies on $XY$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2009

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find the largest subset of $\{-n,-n+1,\ldots,n\}$ containing no three elements $a,b,c$ (not necessarily distinct) with $a+b+c=0$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2009

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: (a) Prove that if a chessboard polygon can be tiled by dominoes, it can be done so tastefully (avoiding two specific configurations). (b) Prove such a tasteful tiling is unique.
figure_description: Distasteful domino configurations and examples of tasteful/non-tasteful tilings
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2009

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Trapezoid $ABCD$ ($AB\parallel CD$) inscribed in $\omega$; $G$ inside $\triangle BCD$. Rays $AG,BG$ meet $\omega$ at $P,Q$; line through $G$ parallel to $AB$ meets $BD,BC$ at $R,S$. Prove $PQRS$ is cyclic iff $BG$ bisects $\angle CBD$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2009

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Nonconstant rational sequences $(s_n),(t_n)$ with $(s_i-s_j)(t_i-t_j)\in\mathbb{Z}$ for all $i,j$. Prove there exists rational $r$ with $(s_i-s_j)r\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $(t_i-t_j)/r\in\mathbb{Z}$ for all $i,j$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2009
